title: SB 1229 (2026 - Fifty-seventh Legislature - Second Regular Session (azleg session id 130)): early voting; identification; emergency voting
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) Sec. 2: Section 16-542, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) Any on-site early voting location or other early voting location shall require each elector to present identification as prescribed in section 16-579 before receiving a ballot.
(section) Sec. 2: Section 16-542, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para E)
(quote) An elector who appears personally not later than 7:00 p.m. on the Friday preceding the election at an on-site early voting location that is established by the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall be given a ballot after presenting identification as prescribed in section 16-579 and shall be allowed to vote at the on-site location.
(section) Sec. 3: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) If the election is a primary, general or special election that includes a federal office and there are outstanding ballots that require identification or ballot signatures to be corrected or confirmed, in addition to the office's regular business hours, the county recorder's and any city or town clerks' offices that have an agreement with a county to be used as locations at which a voter may submit proof of identification shall be open during regular business hours to allow for curing signatures during the Friday and weekend before and the Friday and weekend after the election.
(section) Sec. 3: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) Beginning with the first missing or mismatched signature that is identified after the period of early voting begins through the Monday immediately preceding the election, the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall submit daily to the political parties that are qualified for continued representation on the state ballot an updated list of all voters whose signatures are missing or inconsistent with the voter's signature on the voter's registration record.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (a) A valid form of identification that bears the photograph, name and address of the elector that reasonably appear to be the same as the name and address in the precinct register, including an Arizona driver license, an Arizona nonoperating identification license, a tribal enrollment card or other form of tribal identification or a United States federal, state or local government issued identification.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (a) Require the voter to present identification that complies with paragraph 1 of this subsection.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (b) Confirm that the name and address on the identification reasonably appear to be the same name and address shown on the voter's registration record.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) Sec. 3: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) A. Except for early ballots tabulated as prescribed in section 16-579.02 or received or issued at a voting location after a voter's identification is confirmed as prescribed by section 16-579, subsection A, paragraph 4, on receipt of the envelope containing the early ballot and the mail affidavit, the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall compare the signature on the envelope with the signature of the elector on the elector's registration record as prescribed by section 16-550.01.
(section) Sec. 3: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) If there are no ballots remaining that require identification or signatures to be cured, the county recorder and city and town clerks are not required to be open during the weekend.
(section) Sec. 3: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) If the ballot is a conditional provisional ballot, the voter shall provide proof of identification to the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections not later than the fifth business day after a primary, general or special election that includes a federal office or the third business day after any other election.
(section) Sec. 3: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) Beginning on the Wednesday immediately following the election through the end of the signature cure period after a primary, general or special election that includes a federal office, or the third business day after the election for any other election, the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall submit daily to the political parties that are qualified for continued representation on the state ballot an updated list of all voters whose signatures are inconsistent with the voter's signature on the voter's registration record and all voters who voted with a conditional provisional ballot.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (c) A valid form of identification that bears the photograph, name and address of the elector except that if the address on the identification does not reasonably appear to be the same as the address in the precinct register or the identification is a valid United States military identification card or a valid United States passport and does not bear an address, the identification must be accompanied by one of the items listed in subdivision (b) of this paragraph.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 2)
(quote) 2. If the elector does not present identification that complies with paragraph 1 of this subsection, the elector is only eligible to vote a provisional ballot as prescribed by section 16-584 or a conditional provisional ballot as provided for in the secretary of state's instruction and procedures manual adopted pursuant to section 16-452.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 3)
(quote) 3. until the effective date of this amendment to this section, if the voter surrenders the early ballot to the precinct inspector and the voter is not otherwise required to be issued a provisional ballot, the voter shall be issued a standard ballot after presenting identification pursuant to this subsection.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (c) Stamp the signed mail affidavit with a stamp that reads "ID verified" and place the stamped mail affidavit that contains the early ballot in a secured ballot box that is labeled for early ballots.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 1)
(quote) 1. If the electronic pollbook or other system indicates that the voter's early ballot has not been returned or accepted by the county recorder and the voter is not otherwise required to be issued a provisional ballot, the voter may be issued a standard ballot after presenting identification pursuant to subsection A of this section.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 2)
(quote) 2. If the electronic pollbook or other system indicates that the voter's early ballot has been received or accepted by the county recorder, the voter may not be issued a standard ballot and may only be issued a provisional ballot as prescribed in section 16-584.

(section) Bill text
(quote) REFERENCE TITLE: early voting; identification; emergency voting
(section) Sec. 3: Section 16-550, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para A)
(quote) A. Except for early ballots tabulated as prescribed in section 16-579.02 or received or issued at a voting location after a voter's identification is confirmed as prescribed by section 16-579, subsection A, paragraph 4, on receipt of the envelope containing the early ballot and the mail affidavit, the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall compare the signature on the envelope with the signature of the elector on the elector's registration record as prescribed by section 16-550.01.
(section) Sec. 5: Section 16-572, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para C)
(quote) C. A person shall not take or remove a ballot from the polling place before the polls are closed, except that early ballots that are returned at voting locations on election day after a voter's identification is confirmed as prescribed by section 16-579, subsection a, paragraph 4 may be removed by two authorized election workers who must each be a member of a different one of the two largest political parties, who have completed a chain of custody log maintained at the voting location that includes the total count of the early ballots being transported and who deliver the ballots to a designated receiving site that is an official elections facility and not a third party vendor.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (b) Two different items that contain the name and address of the elector that reasonably appear to be the same as the name and address in the precinct register, including a utility bill, a bank or credit union statement that is dated within ninety days of the date of the election, a valid Arizona vehicle registration, an Arizona vehicle insurance card, an Indian census card, tribal enrollment card or other form of tribal identification, a property tax statement, a recorder's certificate, a voter registration card, a valid United States federal, state or local government issued identification or any mailing that is labeled as "official election material".
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 3)
(quote) 3. until the effective date of this amendment to this section, if the voter surrenders the early ballot to the precinct inspector and the voter is not otherwise required to be issued a provisional ballot, the voter shall be issued a standard ballot after presenting identification pursuant to this subsection.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 4)
(quote) 4. Beginning on the effective date of this amendment to this section, at any voting location during the period of early voting and on election day, the voter may choose to provide identification when presenting the voter's mailed early ballot or when the voter is issued an early ballot, and if so the election official shall:
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) (c) Stamp the signed mail affidavit with a stamp that reads "ID verified" and place the stamped mail affidavit that contains the early ballot in a secured ballot box that is labeled for early ballots.
(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read: (para 1)
(quote) 1. If the electronic pollbook or other system indicates that the voter's early ballot has not been returned or accepted by the county recorder and the voter is not otherwise required to be issued a provisional ballot, the voter may be issued a standard ballot after presenting identification pursuant to subsection A of this section.

(section) Sec. 6: Section 16-579, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended to read:
(quote) Identification is deemed valid unless it can be determined on its face that it has expired.
